displayName: Shared World missions Paint Clearcoat Expanded
description:
Shared World missions Paint Clearcoat Expanded is a procedural-shader-profile added by the final Zaylins gameplay, sensory, environmental, interaction, customization, and cohesion sweep for shared-world. It closes the “missions shader” gap with a named production asset rather than an invisible placeholder, a recycled generic puff, an unrelated object, or a crude primitive approximation. The result must communicate its purpose immediately through silhouette, motion, timing, optical response, state, surface contact, or interaction while following cross-town physical realism, controlled stylization, legible silhouettes, accessibility, and consistent gameplay language.

Required production anatomy: base shading model, normal response, roughness response, view-angle response, lighting response, quality tiers, accessibility controls, editor preview profile. Every component is functional. Components connect through believable supports, timing relationships, strand roots, anatomy, attachment points, projection rules, emitter origins, service paths, collision-safe boundaries, or state transitions appropriate to Shared World missions Paint Clearcoat Expanded. Materials and response layers include shader parameter set, mask or lookup input, lighting integration, fallback material. Separation follows real construction, biological growth, light transport, contamination, weather, particle behavior, hair-fiber behavior, or gameplay state rather than arbitrary color blocks.

Implementation defines a stable named origin, deterministic forward or projection direction, scale envelope, spawn or placement conditions, looping or one-shot lifecycle, transition timing, cleanup and pooling, network relevance, quality tiers, editor-preview metadata, and validation thresholds. Dependencies on surfaces, bodies, vehicles, weapons, water, wind, camera, lighting, audio, quests, or interaction sockets are explicit and testable. Close-range presentation needs convincing breakup, thickness, depth, hardware, strand structure, species anatomy, or layered motion. Distant presentation preserves the primary read without excessive triangles, overdraw, alpha sorting, particle count, shadows, or replication traffic.

Accessibility is mandatory. The asset does not rely on color alone. Flashing, injury feedback, camera motion, particle density, and hazard communication include reduced-flash, reduced-motion, reduced-particle, high-contrast, or icon alternatives where relevant. Injury effects default to non-graphic presentation. Stylized blood is abstract and optional, contains no gore or exposed anatomy, and has paint, spark, dust, and comic-impact alternatives. Hair uses a scalp-conforming root field, purposeful hairline, believable density and gravity, style-specific structure, silhouette variation, ear and nape clearance, recolor support, and secondary-motion planning. Afros are not bunched spheres. Locs are not identical cylinders. Braids and twists show interwoven rhythm, parting, tension, taper, and purposeful styling.

This specification never authorizes crude geometry. Every layer reinforces Shared World missions Paint Clearcoat Expanded, integrates with adjacent Zaylins systems, and passes recognition, lifecycle, town-style, accessibility, performance, and state review. Specialized GLBs remain outside the generic primitive Blender lane until a dedicated builder can satisfy this contract.
designIntent: Close the missions shader gap with Shared World missions Paint Clearcoat Expanded. Preserve its full component, material, lifecycle, accessibility, performance, and state contract without primitive substitutions.
